summary: Authored a source-only unified patch within the four allowed paths that isolates mori-core's only two Midnight dev dependencies (midnight-base-crypto, midnight-serialize) behind a non-default, opt-in feature `midnight-compat-tests`. The crates move from unconditional [dev-dependencies] (which Cargo cannot make optional/feature-gated) to optional [dependencies] referenced via `dep:`, and the single consumer test `signing_frame_matches_pinned_midnight_native_verifier` (tests/intents.rs:64-86) is gated with #[cfg(feature = "midnight-compat-tests")] with its body byte-identical. Default feature set stays empty, so ordinary mori-core consumers and default library behavior are unchanged, no SDK is default-enabled on consumers, and SDK-free selections `cargo test -p mori-core` and `cargo test --frozen -j1 -p mori-core --no-default-features --test continuations -- --test-threads=1` no longer compile the Midnight closure. The exact native test is retained in an explicit, separately qualified matrix: rust.yml keeps `cargo test --workspace --locked` and adds a dedicated feature-enabled step, and RUST_GUIDELINES documents both the SDK-free selection and the explicit compatibility command with its coverage boundary. No runner/scheduler, no new execution/resource permission, no SDK/proof/key/ledger/network access, and Cargo.lock (out of scope) is confirmed unaffected because mori-core's lock dependency array (Cargo.lock:2498-2511) already lists both crates in a flat, kind/optionality-agnostic set.
patch:
diff --git a/crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml b/crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml
--- a/crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml
+++ b/crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml
@@ -4,16 +4,24 @@
 edition.workspace = true
 rust-version.workspace = true
 license.workspace = true
 
+[features]
+# Opt-in and non-default: enables only the Midnight-native signing-frame
+# compatibility test. Ordinary mori-core consumers and SDK-free test
+# selection never pull these dependencies.
+midnight-compat-tests = ["dep:midnight-base-crypto", "dep:midnight-serialize"]
+
 [dependencies]
 mori-lexer.workspace = true
 serde.workspace = true
 serde_json.workspace = true
 thiserror.workspace = true
 sha2.workspace = true
 k256.workspace = true
+# Optional and off by default; pulled in only by the midnight-compat-tests
+# feature for the native compatibility test.
+midnight-base-crypto = { workspace = true, optional = true }
+midnight-serialize = { workspace = true, optional = true }
 
 [dev-dependencies]
 proptest.workspace = true
-midnight-base-crypto.workspace = true
-midnight-serialize.workspace = true
diff --git a/crates/mori-core/tests/intents.rs b/crates/mori-core/tests/intents.rs
--- a/crates/mori-core/tests/intents.rs
+++ b/crates/mori-core/tests/intents.rs
@@ -60,6 +60,7 @@
     let b = mori_core::json::parse(r#"{"a":"1","b":"2"}"#).unwrap();
     assert_eq!(canonical(&a).unwrap(), canonical(&b).unwrap());
 }
+#[cfg(feature = "midnight-compat-tests")]
 #[test]
 fn signing_frame_matches_pinned_midnight_native_verifier() {
     use midnight_serialize::Deserializable;
diff --git a/.github/workflows/rust.yml b/.github/workflows/rust.yml
--- a/.github/workflows/rust.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/rust.yml
@@ -39,4 +39,9 @@ jobs:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
       - name: Test
         run: cargo test --workspace --locked
+      # The default workspace test above runs with default features, so the
+      # feature-gated Midnight-native compatibility test is not selected there.
+      # Run it explicitly so full compatibility coverage is retained.
+      - name: Midnight native compatibility (mori-core/midnight-compat-tests)
+        run: cargo test --locked -p mori-core --features midnight-compat-tests --test intents -- --test-threads=1
diff --git a/RUST_GUIDELINES.md b/RUST_GUIDELINES.md
--- a/RUST_GUIDELINES.md
+++ b/RUST_GUIDELINES.md
@@ -69,4 +69,16 @@
   cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
   cargo test --workspace --locked
   ```
+- `mori-core`'s Midnight-native compatibility test is gated behind the
+  non-default `midnight-compat-tests` feature, so ordinary `mori-core` test
+  selection is free of Midnight dependencies, for example
+  `cargo test -p mori-core` or
+  `cargo test --frozen -j1 -p mori-core --no-default-features --test continuations -- --test-threads=1`.
+  The `cargo test --workspace --locked` above does not enable that feature, so
+  run the compatibility test explicitly for full coverage (it builds the pinned
+  Midnight SDK closure):
+
+  ```
+  cargo test --locked -p mori-core --features midnight-compat-tests --test intents
+  ```
 - The optional `rust` workflow is manual only. Ordinary work does not dispatch
coverageMatrix: ORDINARY SDK-FREE, default features (`cargo test -p mori-core`): compiles only mori-lexer/serde/serde_json/thiserror/sha2/k256 plus proptest; midnight-compat-tests feature OFF so both optional Midnight crates are not resolved/built; the gated test is cfg'd out; the other three intents.rs tests (genuine_signature_and_bound_domain, tampering_expiry_and_noncanonical_encoding_reject, json_order_does_not_change_signing_bytes), continuations.rs and lib tests still run. No Midnight edge.

ORDINARY SDK-FREE, explicit candidate route (`cargo test --frozen -j1 -p mori-core --no-default-features --test continuations -- --test-threads=1`): default set already empty so --no-default-features is a no-op that cannot enable the feature; Midnight optional deps stay disabled; continuations Core/2 API test exercised SDK-free. Retained unchanged.

MIDNIGHT COMPATIBILITY, explicit matrix (`cargo test --locked -p mori-core --features midnight-compat-tests --test intents`): enables optional midnight-base-crypto + midnight-serialize (pinned git closure built); runs the EXACT, unmodified signing_frame_matches_pinned_midnight_native_verifier plus the other three intents tests. This is the separately qualified retention of the original SDK test; its full body is preserved and not faked.

WORKFLOW (.github/workflows/rust.yml, test job): still manual workflow_dispatch only; keeps `cargo test --workspace --locked` (compat OFF, so the gated test is not silently run there) and adds one explicit feature-qualified step running the compat test. No automatic/hosted trigger added; no new runner or scheduler.

GUIDELINES (RUST_GUIDELINES.md Checks): records that ordinary mori-core selection is SDK-free, gives the exact `--features midnight-compat-tests` command for full compatibility coverage, and states the coverage boundary (the feature builds the pinned Midnight SDK closure). No change to fmt/clippy/workspace-test lines.
limitations: Source-only proposal; no shell/Cargo/rustc/clippy/SDK/model/VM/signing/key/proof/wallet/ledger/network/cache access was used and none is authorized. Nothing was built or run; no resource counter touched. Root inspects/applies and independent reviewers judge the exact final candidate before any command.

Cargo.lock is NOT among the four allowed paths and is intentionally unchanged. I verified mori-core's lock entry (candidate/Cargo.lock:2498-2511) lists `midnight-base-crypto` and `midnight-serialize` in a single flat `dependencies` array that does not record dependency kind or optionality, so moving them from dev to optional-normal leaves the resolved graph identical and should satisfy `--frozen`/`--locked`. This is a static inference; root must confirm the actual cargo/toolchain does not demand a lock rewrite. If it did, that would require a 5th path and a changes-required disposition.

Enabling midnight-compat-tests builds the pinned git Midnight SDK closure and its transitive build scripts/proc-macros (e.g. cc, cmake, blst, aws-lc-sys, ring, reqwest and the midnight-* git crates). Those transitive sources, build scripts and compiler/toolchain behavior are UNINSPECTED here; prior reviews classify this as blocked-SDK-native. The SDK-free routes avoid that closure, but ordinary registry dependency build safety is not asserted inspected.

Standard feature-gating consequence: under default features, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace` do NOT compile or lint the gated test body; it is type-checked/executed only under the explicit `--features midnight-compat-tests` command/step. This matches the guideline to keep SDK deps behind a feature; coverage of that test therefore depends on running the added matrix entry.
`dep:` feature syntax requires cargo >= 1.60; the workspace is pinned to Rust 1.99.0 (edition 2024), so this is satisfied, but was not compiled to confirm.

Scope of reading: I inspected TASK-SCOPE.md, MANIFEST.json, the four target files, candidate root Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, mori-core/src/lib.rs, tests/continuations.rs head, mori-lexer/Cargo.toml, authority/AGENTS.md, PR-LOCAL-CHECK-SCOPE.md, TERMINAL-REVIEW.json and the 2026-10-14 SECURITY-REVIEW.md. I did NOT traverse external provenance/private/cache/config. Packet facts and the read of intents.rs confirm the two dev deps are used only by the one named test; I did not exhaustively grep every mori-core source file, relying on those facts.

The added workflow step runs the whole intents target under the feature, which also re-runs the three non-Midnight intents tests (harmless duplication); the exact compatibility test is retained unchanged. No blanket execution/resource permission, no 15min/8GiB envelope, and no 30s-wrapper change is implied or repurposed by this patch.
